content.title: Follow-up recommendations after acute pulmonary embolism (PE)

recommendations.text: Routine clinical evaluation of patients 3–6 months after the acute PE episode is recommended.
recommendations.notes: References cited on page (not transcribed here).

recommendations.text: An integrated model of patient care after PE (involving hospital specialists, appropriately qualified nurses, and primary care physicians) is recommended to ensure optimal transition from hospital to community care.

In symptomatic patients with mismatched perfusion defects persisting on V/Q scan beyond 3 months after acute PE, referral to a PH/CTEPH expert centre is recommended, after taking into account the results of echocardiography, natriuretic peptide levels, and/or CPET.
Further diagnostic evaluation should be considered in patients with persistent or new-onset dyspnoea/exercise limitation after PE.
Further diagnostic evaluation may be considered in asymptomatic patients with risk factors for CTEPH.

footnotes.c: For symptoms suggesting recurrence, bleeding, malignancy, or persistent or new-onset exercise limitation, and to decide on extension of anticoagulant treatment.
footnotes.d: Alternatively, dual-energy CT may be used, if appropriate expertise and resources are available on-site.
